claims.text: The multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy forms a stable passive film that protects its intermetallic phases under benign conditions.
Controlled sliding wear at elevated temperature mechanically removes the alloy's protective passive film.
Passive-film removal exposes intermetallic interfaces to the corrosive environment.
Exposed intermetallic interfaces undergo localized corrosion.
Mechanical abrasion preferentially disrupts the passive film at intermetallic phase boundaries.
Continual exposure of fresh alloy surfaces increases corrosion.
Corrosion-induced increases in roughness and brittleness enhance mechanical wear.
The cyclic interaction between passive-film removal, corrosion, and wear produces synergistic tribocorrosion.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion cause greater total degradation than either isolated wear or isolated corrosion.
The wear rate under simultaneous exposure is higher because surface protection is impaired and mechanical properties are altered.
The corrosion rate under simultaneous exposure is higher because wear continually removes the passive film.
The proposed mechanism applies only where a stable passive film exists initially and the wear and corrosion conditions remain within the relevant service regime.
Conditions outside the stated operational regime may activate different degradation mechanisms.

contradictions.description: The design calls for isolated wear, isolated corrosion, and simultaneous tests while also requiring load, sliding speed, and electrolyte composition to be identical across tests. A corrosion-only test cannot have the same applied sliding parameters without ceasing to be corrosion-only, and a wear-only test cannot have the same corrosive electrolyte exposure without ceasing to be wear-only.
